title: Pipeline-aware KV striping with asynchronous cross-GPU sync for continuous batching
creator: Asha Patil
description: Goal: design and prototype a pipeline-aware KV cache striping strategy that minimizes peak GPU memory usage, supports continuous (streaming) batching, and keeps tail latency low across tensor/pipeline parallel model splits. This ticket covers a new approach that uses deterministic stripe placement, lightweight per-stripe versioning, and asynchronous cross-GPU delta syncs to avoid global stalls during KV writes and evictions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype runs in CI perf cluster with 2x tensor-parallel x 2x pipeline-parallel topology and reduces max per-GPU KV peak by >=20% for long-context tests (8k+ tokens). 2) End-to-end tail (P99) generation latency does not regress more than 15% compared to baseline under continuous batching load. 3) No correctness regressions (model outputs unchanged within tolerance) for canonical prompt set. 4) Includes integration tests that validate stripe versioning and GC under synthetic KV churn.
technical_decision_log: We evaluated three approaches: (A) global KV AllGather on each new write, (B) strict partitioned shards with synchronous barrier, (C) stripe+async-delta with epoched versions. Approach C chosen because it balances memory peak reduction with low per-request latency. Key decisions: use per-stripe sequence numbers + compacted delta lists; prefer NCCL-based async peer-to-peer where NVLink is available and fallback to RDMA or host-mediated memcpy when not; avoid global barriers during continuous batching by making reads consult a small per-stripe metadata table to resolve most-recent version.
design_notes: - Stripe assignment: round-robin by KV key hash across pipeline stages to keep pipeline-local reads fast. - Versioning: 32-bit epoch + 8-bit subversion per stripe to enable quick merges. - Sync model: asynchronous push of deltas from owner GPU to replica GPUs using non-blocking NCCL AllReduce-like patterns. - Eviction: cooperative eviction policy where owner emits tombstones and replicas garbage-collect once local epoch observed. - Memory compaction: periodic in-place compaction of delta lists triggered when fragmentation > 25% or free memory < threshold. - Continuous batching: maintain lightweight per-request KV read cache to avoid multiple GPU fetches for tokens that share prefixes in the same batch. - Fallback correctness: if async sync fails or version mismatch detected, the request can request a synchronous fetch for that stripe, with a configurable retry budget.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): implement stripe metadata and deterministic assignment; add per-stripe version counters and small in-memory index. Phase 2 (3w): implement async delta push/merge path using NCCL non-blocking primitives and host fallback; unit tests for merges. Phase 3 (2w): eviction and compaction logic + stress tests under continuous batching harness. Phase 4 (2w): perf tuning on CI cluster, integrate with runtime batching scheduler, add observability (per-stripe metrics, evictions, sync latency).
risks: - Async delta model can lead to short-lived divergence causing rare synchronous fetch fallbacks which may spike tail latency. - Complexity of multi-codepath (NVLink vs RDMA vs host) increases maintenance burden. - Wrong stripe assignment heuristics could increase cross-stage traffic and negate memory benefits. - GC bugs could cause memory leaks or stale KV reads if tombstones mishandled.
mitigations: - Conservative initial rollout behind a feature flag with telemetry to measure sync fallbacks and divergence rate. - Add strong integration tests simulating node loss and network jitter. - Start with small stripe counts and run ablation to choose heuristic. - Implement tombstone TTL and a guarded GC only when all replicas report epoch >= tombstone epoch.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for stripe index, versioning, and merge correctness. - Integration tests: synthetic long-context generation, continuous streaming batches, forced failure of async sync to validate fallback. - Performance bench: run 50k-step generation across several model sizes and measure per-GPU peak memory, token throughput, and P50/P95/P99 latency. - Canary: rollout to a small dedicated cluster for 48h with monitoring dashboard for KV sync latency and evictions.
observability: Emit metrics: stripe_mem_usage_bytes, stripe_fragmentation_ratio, stripe_last_epoch, stripe_sync_latency_ms, stripe_sync_failures, kv_sync_fallbacks_count. Instrument logs with stripe-id and epoch on merges and tombstones. Add tracing span for cross-GPU syncs for distributed tracing.
notes: Related research: prior internal experiments showed that naive AllGather causes a 2-3x increase in per-GPU KV peak under pipelined PP; this design aims to reduce that by striping and only syncing deltas. Consider future work to integrate with quantized KV encodings to further reduce memory cost.
